hook.text: Google bought YouTube in 2006 for $1.65 billion. Critics said it was absurdly overpriced.

buildup.text: YouTube was 18 months old with 100 million daily video views, zero profit, and massive copyright lawsuit risk.

discovery.text: Google saw what others missed: video would dominate the internet. Owning the platform meant owning the future of media.

twist.text: YouTube lost money for years. Google subsidized it with search profits until advertising finally made it profitable.

climax.text: The best acquisitions look expensive on day one and cheap by year ten.

punchline.text: $1.65 billion in 2006, $31 billion yearly now. The best deal ever.

quiz.question: Why was Google's purchase of YouTube initially criticized?
options: The $1.65 billion price seemed too high for a young, unprofitable platform
